findings.title: Received protection becomes protection owed
findings.claim: Because the focus names the orphan as a child who has lost the protecting parent and forbids overpowering him, the command can be heard as regulating the transfer of power: protection received by the addressee becomes protection owed to the exposed child, not force directed downward.
findings.mechanism: The ytm B001 focus carrier supplies the lost-protector vulnerability and the qhr B001 carrier supplies overpowering from above. The supplied 93:6 shelter recollection and direct wider orphan-treatment parallels return through those focus words, changing the command from an isolated ban into a rule against reproducing the hierarchy that shelter had answered.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why the remembered orphanhood matters here: being sheltered changes what one may do when one later stands above another vulnerable person.
findings.containment: The plain prohibition against oppressing the orphan remains intact. This finding infers a transfer of responsibility from the supplied role change; it does not turn the imperative into a complete care program. The reader support's unresolved mercy citation is not promoted to an additional branch.

epistemic.reason: A trusted citable focus finding supplies the two core carriers, while the represented legacy walks and target-morphology-limited connection rows support the wider role-transfer inference with explicit qualification.
